name: The Public-Source Intelligence Bureau
tagline: Make a business-technology judgment that can be traced back to every included row.
mission: Investigate a fictional offline-kiosk launch using original synthetic public-style notices, release notes, lab notes, and benchmark rows. Separate claims from verification, compare competing hypotheses, expose contradictions and uncertainty, and prepare a decision-gated next investigation.

teams.name: Collection and Provenance
teams.purpose: Maintain a bounded local corpus and exact file/row citations, with no live collection or private data.

teams.name: Timeline and Analysis
teams.purpose: Reconstruct chronology and distinguish announcement scope from demonstrated technical behavior.

teams.name: Competing Hypotheses
teams.purpose: Test alternative explanations and challenge confidence without counting correlated sources as independent votes.

teams.name: Verification
teams.purpose: Reproduce benchmark arithmetic, audit references, and classify unresolved conflicts and measurement gaps.

teams.name: Decision Briefing
teams.purpose: Deliver a bounded recommendation, uncertainties, and explicit owner decision gates.

case.title: Can fictional Juniper Queue support an unattended offline pilot on 15 October?
case.brief: SYNTHETIC investigation as of 2026-09-17. A fictional business is considering a 72-hour disconnected kiosk pilot on 2026-10-15. Included public-style documents disagree about offline scope, launch readiness, and event recovery. No real company, confidential intelligence, private individual, or real published source is represented.
success_criteria: Every assertion in a decision brief cites an exact included file and CSV row, with provenance hashes reproducible by the offline index.
Eighteen source records across five files, nine coded claims, and three conflict/ambiguity cases are accounted for.
The investigation distinguishes acknowledgment from recovered event durability and identifies the eight-ID gap in the six-hour restart row.
No included run is represented as a successful 72-hour offline restart test; source correlations and synthetic-data limitations remain explicit.
The final output is a conditional investigation/decision recommendation, not procurement approval or a claim that the fictional product is launch-ready.

tasks.title: Freeze the bounded synthetic corpus
tasks.instructions: Inventory the five source files and the question's as-of date. Record provenance, authored-source type, limitations, and exclusion of live collection.
acceptance: Lists five explicit files and eighteen uniquely identified records, all SYNTHETIC.
Treats vendor-authored items as one origin group and the lab-style notes as another, without claiming statistical independence.

tasks.title: Build the offline evidence index
tasks.instructions: Run the authored index and audit utility and its tests. Save a reviewable index with exact citations and content hashes; do not fetch sources or execute any source content.
acceptance: Every source citation resolves to a declared file and physical CSV row, header counted as row 1.
Every coded claim and conflict reference resolves; duplicate IDs and future-dated evidence are rejected.

tasks.title: Reconstruct promise, preview, and correction chronology
tasks.instructions: Generate the local timeline and annotate changes in claim scope through the as-of date. Separate announcement date, proposed launch date, and measurement date.
acceptance: Shows the 1 September promise, 8 September credential condition, 12 September workaround, 14 September undated fix, and 17 September missing long-run evidence.
Does not infer an observed launch or a confirmed schedule from future-facing text.

tasks.title: Compare full-offline, supervised-only, and schedule-slip explanations
tasks.instructions: Review the supplied hypothesis definitions and claim coding. Build a qualitative evidence matrix with disconfirming observations and evidence that would change the assessment; do not convert row counts to probabilities.
acceptance: Covers all three hypotheses with supporting, contradictory, and non-discriminating evidence.
Explicitly treats the lack of a dated fix as uncertainty rather than proof of a delay.

tasks.title: Audit acknowledgments, restart conditions, and recovered IDs
tasks.instructions: Recompute each run from the included rows and reconcile the lab-style statements. Keep different durations and restart conditions separate; blank recovery measurements mean unknown, not zero.
acceptance: Reports 987/1000 for the no-restart run; 0/400 for each 36-hour blocked restart; 398/400 acknowledgments and 390 recovered IDs for the six-hour run.
Identifies eight acknowledged-but-unreconciled IDs in the six-hour run and no measured 72-hour pass.
Does not pool unlike scenarios into a reliability estimate.

tasks.title: Classify contradictions and metric mismatches
tasks.instructions: Review each conflict pair against the exact included rows, the hypotheses, and benchmark audit. Distinguish direct scope conflicts from schedule ambiguity and measurement mismatches.
acceptance: Covers all three supplied conflict cases with citations, unresolved questions, and a falsifiable resolution request.
Does not call unlike acknowledgment and durability metrics a demonstrated direct contradiction.

tasks.title: Turn uncertainty into a prospective investigation board
tasks.instructions: Prioritize the supplied inquiry rows using the conflict ledger. Define the next safe public artifact or synthetic test specification needed and who reviews it; no live collection occurs in this task.
acceptance: Includes a 72-hour cold-restart test, acknowledged/recovered-ID reconciliation, exact release identification, and source-independence question.
Every inquiry has an owner, stopping condition, and decision dependency; any actual collection or contact remains approval-gated.

tasks.title: Draft a source-cited bounded decision brief
tasks.instructions: Use the briefing structure to answer the specific pilot question. Separate authored facts, document claims, inferences, and unknowns; offer conditional paths rather than unsupported certainty.
acceptance: Every material statement has a file/row citation or is explicitly labeled inference/unknown.
Does not endorse an unattended 72-hour pilot on the present corpus; any supervised alternative states its limitations and owner gate.

tasks.title: Challenge the brief's strongest and weakest conclusions
tasks.instructions: Attempt to explain the evidence under each alternative hypothesis. Identify overclaims, correlated corroboration, missing measurements, and what new evidence would reverse the recommendation.
acceptance: Names at least one falsifier for the preferred explanation and one reason not to overstate schedule slip.
Checks that synthetic source text is not misrepresented as a real publication or independent certification.

tasks.title: Issue the investigation handoff and owner gate
tasks.instructions: Resolve or explicitly retain each challenge, and issue a final investigation handoff. Record what the corpus supports and what evidence/approval must exist before a real pilot or commercial decision.
acceptance: Includes as-of date, confidence limitations, unresolved inquiries, and exact review triggers.
Authorizes no contact, procurement, deployment, identity lookup, private collection, or cross-organization access.
